title: 胸有成竹 — Why Did a Painter Plant Bamboo Outside His Window?
hook: Why Did a Painter Plant Bamboo Outside His Window?
caption: 胸有成竹 (xiōng yǒu chéng zhú): have the finished bamboo in your mind before you paint. Northern Song painter Wen Tong studied bamboo through every season, and his cousin Su Shi wrote down his method. Today it means having a well-thought-out plan before you act.
description:
胸有成竹 (xiōng yǒu chéng zhú), literally "a finished bamboo in the chest", means having a well-thought-out plan before you act, and so acting with calm confidence.

The saying comes from the Northern Song painter Wen Tong (文同), famous for lifelike ink bamboo. He planted bamboo outside his window and studied it across seasons and weather. His rule — 故画竹必先得成竹于胸中 — was recorded by his cousin, the poet Su Shi (苏轼), in 《文与可画筼筜谷偃竹记》.

Example: 面对这次复杂的谈判，他早已胸有成竹。Facing this complex negotiation, he already had a well-prepared plan in mind.
